method: Read scope/taxpapers-result.json and -checklist.json, docs/verification/audit/papers.json's rows, tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts in full, git diff of src/engine/systems/statetax.ts, taxreturn.ts, lending.ts, guide/taxes.ts, guide/papers.ts and the four outside tests. Ran tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts alone (13 passed). Probed one claim outside the repo (scratchpad/probe/nr.probe.ts, a vitest config rooted in the scratchpad): an international (born in London) life for each family, figuresFor 2026 and 2027. Nothing in the repository was edited.

rows.disposition: Mostly played and sound; one downstream the row names (a state plan ended paid by Pay) is evidenced only on a fixture, though a student reaches it
problems: The row's downstream names 'a state plan ended paid' (audit downstream, kept by the result's rowText.downstream). applyStatePayment ends a plan paid when Pay clears what's owed outside it (src/engine/systems/statetax.ts:358-362). No test on the student's life does it: the Connecticut plan in tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts:352 is paid off by its own payments (how 'plan'), not by tax.pay_state. The only evidence is tests/liens-and-arrangements.test.ts:221-224, a Pennsylvania life whose balance is put on by hand (owing()). It is reachable by play: a student's Connecticut plan in force, then Pay on Papers. One assertion closes it.

tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts:296-297: the comment works the bill as $585.33 + $58.53 + $5.85, which is $649.71, but asserts $649.72. The engine rounds the whole and gives interest the remainder ($5.86) (statetax.ts:212-213). So the literal is the engine's rounding, not worked independently from 12-735. Under 12-735, 1% of $585.33 is $5.85 and the bill would be $649.71. It's a one-cent rounding defect, and the comment contradicts its own assertion.

tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts:328 and :341 ('the levy … off the calendar', 'no levy after') don't first show a levy pending on this life before the payment. The scheduled levy is shown only on another life (the levied() twin at :428-432). The expectations are non-vacuous only by inference.

The fix (statetax.ts:381, `Math.max(sim.now, r.due)`) applies to every state, though it cites only Connecticut's statutes. tests/state-tax.test.ts, state-tax-states.test.ts and tax-places.test.ts were moved for California, Georgia and Indiana with no source of their own. r.due is the federal return's due date, which for a 1040-NR with no wages is 15 June (taxreturn.ts:880, :1241). Connecticut's own due date is 15 April. For such a year, Connecticut's notices now wait for the IRS's date. This is an edge case, and accrual already read r.due before the change.
weakTests: PLAYER JOURNEY: filed on 1 February unpaid, Connecticut’s bill waits for the 18 April due date … $649.72 … (the bill literal is the engine's whole-rounding; its comment's parts sum to $649.71)

rows.disposition: Genuinely unreachable: confirmed by reading every writer figuresFor reads
problems: Confirmed. These all write to the year of the moment they pay: recordWages, recordBenefit, recordInterest, recordPension and recordScholarship (src/engine/systems/earnings.ts:131-271), school.ts's withholding (:2997, :3209), the IRS's refund interest (taxreturn.ts:1627) and health premiums (health.ts:592). figuresFor's other inputs are fixed once the year ends: residence, nonresidentFor, the year's tables and the poverty line (taxreturn.ts:883-1036). Only wages carry a `where`, and only the two school.ts wage writers exist (:3226, :3797), neither with one. The test shows it on one life, and the code holds it for all.

rows.disposition: Played on the student's defaulted IRS plan through Papers and the command, its readers checked across a reload

Played. The armCollection fix is real and its test fails without it (thaw → loadSave arms collection while the plan is in default, and the end adds a second TAX_NOTICE). The surviving redundant cancel is disclosed.
Played: asked on Papers, paid to the end, missed and ended, refused (months, second plan, a levied year still owed). The statePlanRefusal fix is real and tested by play.
problems: tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts:366-370: on 1 May the parts are asserted as interest $4.87, where 1% of $487.77 is $4.88. The comment says this is the engine's whole-rounding, so the literal follows the engine's convention, not 12-735 cent by cent. This is the same one-cent artifact as tax.pay_state's $649.72, and it doesn't change the verdict.

rows.disposition: Genuinely unreachable: every life files in Connecticut only, and its cure is 'none'
problems: Reachability checked. homeOf is person.currentLocationId (earnings.ts:284), and nothing writes it after creation (guide/day.ts:16; grep finds no assignment). Neither wage writer passes `where`, so y.elsewhere stays empty, and the state lines come from byResidence alone (taxreturn.ts:927-930). The probe agrees: an international life of every family files in us-ct only.

rows.disposition: Played on the student's Connecticut lien: shut until paid (rendered), asked once on Papers, refused twice, released 30 days on across a reload, with no levy after
problems: The 'no levy after' expectation (tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts:341) would also pass if no levy had been due. It is supported by the levied twin at :428-432, not by this life.

rows.disposition: Genuinely unreachable for Connecticut: confirmed by reading lienInError and the assessment
problems: Confirmed. assessStateNonFiler takes the return's own state figure (statetax.ts:807-831). reconsiderState replaces it with the same figure. Connecticut's order (penalty, interest, tax) leaves the tax unpaid while anything is owed, so tax paid before a lien is filed is always less than the balance (lienInError, statetax.ts:700-706).

rows.disposition: Genuinely unreachable: a student's IRS year owes under $2,000 against the $10,000 threshold
problems: Checked across families by the probe. The largest IRS balance on a played year is the Scraping family's $1,700.39 (2027). An international life owes $345.00 at most (wealthy/inherited 2027), and the needy ones get a refund.

rows.disposition: Genuinely unreachable: only Oregon charges it, and no life files there (see tax.catch_up_state_plan's reachability check)
Overstated: the W-7 reader is reachable by play but is evidenced only on TEST SETUP income
problems: The result says every reader that changes an outcome is 'tested by play' and that 'No income was invented'. The W-7 reader is the 1040-NR refund held seven weeks more without a number (taxreturn.ts:1522-1527, refunds only). Its test, tests/evidence-g17-papers.test.ts:722-746, invents income: 'TEST SETUP: $3,000 more of work-study with $600 withheld' (:726), withholding that Yale's work-study payroll never takes in play (school.ts:3222-3224).

That refund is reachable by play. Probe (scratchpad/probe/nr.probe.ts): a London-born student of the nothing, scraping, modest or comfortable family has 2026 1040-NR owedTo.irs = -$329.56 and 2027 -$411.73, from the 14% withheld on her taxable scholarship. A played needy international life would show the 21 days against the 70 with no setup. The reader is reachable and not played, so the row is partial.

The IRS plan reader (online vs Form 9465) is tested with emptyBank TEST SETUP (tests/evidence-g17-papers.test.ts:753). That state is reachable by play, through a CD as scope-taxpapers does, but the test doesn't play it. This is weaker than claimed, though the flip itself (card vs no card) is played.

Discover's wage test holds as claimed. wagesLastMonth counts 'salary' postings in 30 days (lending.ts:397-409). Work-study (200 hours a year at $23, paid weekly) and the Summer Cabaret's $375 a week, net, can't reach $2,083.33 in 30 days.
weakTests: a 1040-NR filed with the card in hand is processed in the IRS’s 21 days; without it the W-7 holds it seven weeks more, 70 (TEST SETUP income where a played needy international life has the refund)
the IRS’s payment plan on her 1040-NR’s $165.60: with the card come, applied for online … (TEST SETUP empty bank)
